top.title: 49ers game grades: Potent offense outscores fierce Cowboys comeback attempt
top.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. and guard Dominick Puni celebrate a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers raised their record to an NFC-best 8-1 in the offensive showcase everyone expected, going up against the Cowboys in Dallas. The Niners scored 46 points on six touchdowns in their win , getting a personal record performance from Brock Purdy , and showing a readiness to fend off a ferocious Cowboys rally. Offense: A Expectations that Sunday would be a track meet were certainly met by the offense. Christian McCaffrey busted out for 223 total yards and three touchdowns on 17 touches, Deebo Samuel added 109 and two more scores, and Kaelon Black added a sixth trip to the end zone with 66 yards on 13 touches. Purdy's 389 passing yards were a career high, while passing for three touchdowns (two to McCaffrey, one to Samuel) despite getting sacked five times. In addition to getting Samuel back in action, new wideout Keenan Allen made five catches on seven targets in his Niners debut. Defense: D+ About that track meet, yeah, the defense held up its end as well, surrendering 40 points while registering just one sack and one turnover (Malik Mustapha's interception) and allowing 439 yards and letting Dallas score on all three of its red-zone opportunities. That said, there were moments where the defense almost made a big difference that hinted at the unit's potential at full strength; they registered 10 hits on Cowboys QB Dak Prescott, Dre Greenlaw almost made a second-quarter interception on a play where Nick Bosa was in Prescott's face and Fred Warner - who led the team with 11 tackles - forced what looked like a late-game fumble that ultimately wasn't called. Special teams: B As much as this might be a "do no harm" area during a week where the opposing offenses were trading haymakers, the important news is that Eddy Piñeiro didn't miss a kick, making all five extra-point attempts and his lone field-goal attempt. But added credit to Samuel for recovering the inevitable onside kick attempt with 43 seconds left after Dallas narrowed affairs to a single score, and to punter Corliss Waitman for burying the Cowboys on their own 9-yard line on his kick with just 21 seconds left. This was the kind of game where those things mattered. Coaching: B+ Kyle Shanahan 's offense was certainly ready to exploit the Cowboys' porous defense and show it has some big-play ability at any age, while Raheem Morris' defense delivered a fairly respectable game until giving up three fourth-quarter touchdowns. This might seem generous given that late struggle, but ultimately, the 49ers were ready to outscore an electric offense. Overall: B Just that? CeeDee Lamb and the Dallas Cowboys reached 40 points for the first time this season in Week 10 against the San Francisco 49ers. Unfortunately, it still wasn’t enough as the Cowboys lost a 46-40 shootout to the NFC-leading Niners . The Cowboys scored three touchdowns in the fourth quarter, including one by Lamb with less than a minute left in the game, to make the score a bit more respectable. Shortly after scoring that touchdown, Lamb was about ready to leave the building. Per Cowboys beat writer Calvin Watkins, Lamb left the locker room before reporters were allowed in . But despite Lamb’s impressive individual stats, there might be some frustration setting in for the star wide receiver amid another disappointing loss for Dallas. On the bright side, the 4-6 Cowboys are still in the mix in the NFC East after the New York Giants’ loss on Thursday night. top.title: Cris Collinsworth says Bengals' fans are noticing Tee Higgins limping
top.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins was injured during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. Higgins grabbed his leg after a catch, and went to the sideline. He limped noticeably after an incompletion shortly before halftime, but stayed in the game and had a 14-yard catch on the next play. "He has been limping a little bit, and I'm sure Bengals' fans are paying attention," NBC analyst Cris Collinsworth said during the broadcast. Higgins celebrated the 50th TD catch of his NFL career by handing the ball to an excited young fan during the team's NFL Week 9 win against Atlanta. Higgins helped teammate Ja'Marr Chase celebrate his touchdown with a nod to Spanish bullfighting . Higgins was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort in Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in NFL Week 8 against Tennessee. It was Higgins' first career AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 receiving yards against the Titans, and caught two of quarterback Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes . After being held without a catch during the first half, Higgins went off during the second half of a Week 7 rout in Baltimore, catching six Joe Burrow passes for 148 receiving yards with a touchdown. Earlier in the second half, Higgins' shoulder and arm were evaluated by medical personnel after he absorbed a big hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton after a catch. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. Against the Jaguars, Higgins got up slowly after a 19-yard catch near the sideline from Burrow . Higgins got up, but then took a knee. Higgins returned to the game later in the drive, and made a catch on his first play back in the game. He was not on the field for the Bengals' final drive of the game. Higgins had a game-high 10 catches for 140 receiving yards before the injury. He added a 17-yard catch, giving him a total of 157 receiving yards, second only to the 194-yard game he had against Baltimore in 2021. Higgins made a remarkable touchdown catch from quarterback Burrow late in the second quarter of the team's Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. It was among the most impressive NFL catches by Higgins . In March 2025, Higgins agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team. Higgins, Cincinnati's second-round pick in the 2020 NFL draft, is entering his seventh NFL season. top.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper (2) reacts to making a 3-point basket during the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Salt Lake City. (AP Photo/Tyler Tate) (Tyler Tate/Associated Press) With the lowly Utah Jazz threatening to put an end to the Spurs' 12-game winning streak in the fourth quarter Sunday, one thought when through Dylan Harper's mind. "It's time to take over," the Spurs guard said. "It's time to win." Done and done. Harper scored 18 of his career-best 31 points in the final frame to help the Spurs stave off the spirited Jazz 110-102 at the Delta Center. With the victory, the Spurs (12-2) clinched their longest winning streak since 2015-16. They won 11 in a row on two occasions last season. Victor Wembanyama scored 21 of his 26 points in the first half, adding 10 rebounds, six assists and five blocks to the winning effort. Stephon Castle chipped in 20 points and nine assists, while Keldon Johnson muscled his way to an 11-point, 10-rebound double-double off the bench. On paper, Utah hardly looked like the team to give the Spurs' latest winning streak a scare. The Jazz entered Sunday having lost 11 in a row, every bit as cold as the Spurs have been hot. Utah was once again without its All-Star frontcourt of Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Jusuf Nurkic and Jaxson Hayes were also sidelined, leaving Mo Bamba to make his first start since April 2025 with Orlando. San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama dunks during the first half of an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Salt Lake City. (AP Photo/Tyler Tate) (Tyler Tate/Associated Press) Bamba, who had not attempted a 3-pointer this season before Sunday, went 6-of-6 from beyond the arc on his way to 26 points. He was 10 of 13 from the field. Rookie guard Darryn Peterson added 17 points, and the Jazz found themselves with a four-point lead with 5:25 remaining. That's when Harper decided he had seen enough. The 20-year-old became the fifth player in Spurs history to record a 30-point game before his 21st birthday, joining Tony Parker, Jeremy Sochan, Wembanyama and Castle. Harper made six of his eight shots in the fourth quarter and all four of his free throws, repeatedly answering the Jazz whenever they threatened to pull away. His 3-pointer from the left wing brought the Spurs within 98-97 with 3:18 to play. The Spurs never trailed again, escaping with a victory that kept their winning streak intact. top.title: Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker motivated by his late brother
top.description: When we went to talk with Jaquan Brisker in the locker room after their Week 1 win against the Falcons, Channel 11 Sports Director Jenna Harner noticed a T-shirt hanging in his locker with a picture of a young Gateway football player wearing No. 3. We learned it’s his older brother, Tale, who died when Jaquan was just 15 years old. In a raw and open conversation, Brisker shared with Harner how much of an impact Tale had on his life, and why his older brother is one of the main reasons he’s here today. It’s hard to put into words just how much Brisker looks up to his older brother. Growing up, the two were inseparable. “We all thought we was rock stars,” Brisker said. “So all of us, we had this camera. ... We would do all these videos. We were in a rap group or whatever and just be singing different things, dancing and stuff like that. They also played a lot of sports, from football to basketball, roughhoused even more. Tale, who was four years older, always made sure to take his younger brother under his wing. “What was your relationship like just the two of you?” Harner asked. “Yeah, it was amazing,” Brisker said. “‘Cause to be honest, I was in the shadow. I was always shy and things like that. And he was the one to bring me out that comfort zone. But on an early February day in 2015, Brisker’s world was forever changed. He was at a lift, and was confused when his family tried to call him during school. When he arrived at his coach’s house where he was staying, his dad’s car was outside. “When I see him, the first thing I thought, I literally said to him, I’m like, oh, I’m like ‘(Expletive) something’s going on. Something’s wrong,’” Brisker said. Tale was shot and killed in his apartment in Prairie View, Texas. He was just 19 years old. “I remember taking the dog out and then just breaking down crying right there,” Brisker said. “And then I think I probably cried that whole trip to my aunt. And then walked in, hugged my aunt. And then my mom was upstairs. Everybody was torn apart.” “What was the hardest part for you after he passed?” Harner asked. “The toughest part is hearing my mom cry the whole time, and yeah, that was tough. That was tough the whole time,” Brisker said. The last conversation he had with his older brother is one Brisker will never forget. Tale told Jaquan that if anyone in the family was going to make it, it would be him. “Obviously he was telling me to be smart, know, stay in school, you know, just follow in the right direction, things like that,” Brisker said. “And then he knew I love football so much ‘cause obviously we always talked and I always thought my brothers would make it to the NFL, things like that. top.description: CBF mourns the passing of Dino Sani, 1958 World Cup winner Dino Sani, a 1958 World Cup winner, has died at 94 Credits: CBF The Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) deeply mourns the passing of Dino Sani, the former midfielder and 1958 World Cup winner, who died this Sunday (15) at the age of 94. He was part of the first Brazil team to take the country to the pinnacle of world football. “We have lost one of our first world champions. Dino Sani etched his name into the history of the Brazilian national team in 1958. His name will forever stand among the greats of the Amarelinha. At this difficult time for his family and friends, I offer my condolences and pay tribute to this great champion and idol,” said CBF president Samir Xaud. Dino played 24 matches for Brazil, recording 16 wins, four draws and four defeats. He scored four goals. At the 1958 World Cup, he played in the first two matches, against Austria (a 3–0 win) and England (a goalless draw). A muscle injury then ruled him out of the rest of the tournament, and Zito took his place. In addition to the World Cup, he helped win the Oswaldo Cruz Cup (1958), the Bernardo O'Higgins Cup (1959) and the Roca Cup (1960). 1958_06_08_Brazil 3–0 Austria_STANDING De Sordi, Dino Sani, Bellini, Nilton Santos, Orlando, Gilmar. top.title: Louisville Crushes #4 UConn 69-51
top.description: Louisville has a veteran-heavy team and when you have returning players it’s easy to compare them to seasons past. Last year the Cards could jump out to big leads but it often seemed like they’d fold in the 3rd quarter. Tonight Louisville withstood every run, kept their foot on the gas, and dominated the Huskies the entire game in front of a crowd of 12, 692. Imari Berry led all scorers with 21 points. Tajianna Roberts had 11 points but more interestingly she also had 8 rebounds. Both Zamareya Jones and Mackenly Randolph had 10 points and 9 rebounds respectively. Tajianna Roberts said, “In the huddle we kept saying that it’s 0-0 and to not play the score. Take it one play at a time. We weren’t worried about how much we were up. We knew they were capable of making runs so we were just playing as if it was 0-0.” She added, “We stayed composed. I think we’ve learned as vets now as Juniors.” Imari Berry added, “We believed in each other. We came back and we knew what we needed to do and I feel like we’re standing on business.” Coach Walz was impressed with his team’s play especially in rebounding. “I was really proud of the way we competed from start to finish. We talked to everybody about the importance of rebounding the basketball. It was going to take the entire team we can’t just rely on E [Elif Istanbulluoglu] or Mack. It takes everybody. I thought it’s the best effort we’ve had top to bottom.” He added, “Zam and Taj rebounding the basketball were elite. We only gave up 7 offensive boards. They missed 40 shots— 21 of 61 from the field— and we only gave up 7 offensive boards. That’s as good as it gets.” He talked about the importance of getting Mackenly and Elif back after injuries. “Mack and E are our 2 most important players on our team. Hands down. And it’s not because they’re going to score 20. It’s because they communicate and they talk the entire time… They’re directing everybody and they might not always get the credit but they’re why defensively we were as good as we were.” He also praised Imari, “It’s what Imari does. She’s special. She’s a kid who’s continued to work on her game we knew this coming out of high school but it was just a matter of getting her to believe how good she really is. I’m not sure she really understands how good she is…. top.description: Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick was injured during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . top.title: Collinsworth slams Jordan Battle for Bengals-Steelers taunting penalty
top.description: NBC Sports analyst and former Cincinnati Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth blasted defensive back Jordan Battle for his unsportsmanlike conduct/ taunting penalty during the second quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' loss to Jacksonville because of a hamstring injury. Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. He played in all 51 of the Bengals' games over his first three seasons, recording six interceptions and making 30 starts. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of the Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss . Battle was injured during the fourth quarter of the Bengals' Week 13 loss to Pittsburgh last season. During the 2024 season, Battle recovered a fumble and returned it during the third quarter of the Bengals' NFL Week 15 win against Tennessee, but Battle lost the ball just shy of the goal line through the back of the end zone for a touchback. Play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico missed the Week 9 Sunday night game between the Bucs and Bears in Chicago because of a health issue . Noah Eagle called the Bucs-Bears game with Collinsworth and sideline reporter Melissa Stark. NBC Sports analyst Devin McCourty said during the week that he was eager to see the reception for former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin at Paycor Stadium. "I'm excited to see if Mike Tomlin gets booed this week, if people hate him, or are throwing things at him," McCourty told reporters Nov. 11. In 2024, Tirico referred to the tackle then- Bengals linebacker Logan Wilson made in 2023 of Ravens tight end Mark Andrews as a "hip-drop tackle." In an exclusive Q&A in 2022 with The Enquirer, Tirico talked about working with Collinsworth, why the Wild Card Playoff win against the Las Vegas Raiders was the most memorable Bengals game he's called, and his long-time friendship with Bengals radio play-by-play announcer Dan Hoard. top.title: St. Charles falls in OHSAA Division I boys soccer state final
top.description: Another deep tournament run ended in unfortunately familiar fashion for the St. Charles soccer team. The Cardinals almost tripled Kettering Fairmont in shots and earned a handful of quality scoring chances in the Division I boys state final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, but the first-time state finalist Firebirds converted a higher percentage of opportunities and came away with a 3-1 win. Senior forward Sam Lofthouse scored St. Charles’ only goal, spinning and shooting from about 25 yards to the right of the goal with 25:35 to play and sneaking his shot into the upper right corner. That made it 2-1, but Fairmont (15-5-3) got the goal back less than four minutes later. Gavin Weaver’s corner kick got all the way through traffic, and Luke Davidson put it in from right in front. Azariyah Nsabimama and Aaron Black scored 12 minutes apart in the first half for Fairmont, and St. Charles lost for only the fourth time this season (18-4-1) and first since its regular-season finale Oct. 15 against Worthington Kilbourne. St. Charles, appearing in its 12th state tournament, fourth in a row and seeking its first title since 1985, outshot Fairmont 23-8. The Cardinals also were state runners-up in 2024, 2016, 1991, 1988 and 1981. St. Charles had outscored its first five tournament opponents 15-3, including a 1-0 win over defending state champion Dublin Jerome in a state semifinal in which Lofthouse had the only goal. Cardinals sophomore goalie Micah Neil made three saves. Fairmont’s Carson Dewald stopped six shots. This story will be updated. High school sports reporter Dave Purpura can be reached at dpurpura@dispatch.com and at @dp_dispatch on X. nigeria.title: Diabetes: CAPPA urges FG, states to impose 20% sugary drinks tax, reform food policies
nigeria.description: By Chioma Obinna On this day World Diabetes Day, the Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Saturday called on the Federal Government and state governments to urgently reform Nigeria’s food policies, impose a minimum 20 per cent tax on sugar-sweetened beverages and tighten regulations on unhealthy food products to curb the rising burden of diabetes. The organisation warned that efforts to tackle the disease would yield limited results if government focused on screening and treatment while allowing aggressive marketing, widespread availability and affordability of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks to continue unchecked. Making the call in a message to mark the 2026 World Diabetes Day, marked November 14, with the theme, “Early Action on Diabetes”, CAPPA said Nigeria faced an escalating diabetes crisis that required decisive government intervention beyond public awareness and individual lifestyle changes. According to the organisation, Nigeria has the highest number of adults aged 20 to 79 living with diabetes in Africa, while nearly three in four adults with diabetes across the continent remain undiagnosed. It warned that delayed diagnosis exposes millions of Nigerians to potentially life-threatening complications, including kidney failure, blindness, stroke and amputations. CAPPA also raised the alarm over the financial burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases, citing an estimated N1.92 trillion annual out-of-pocket expenditure by Nigerian households on their treatment. Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said diabetes prevention should not be reduced to individual discipline when commercial interests and unhealthy food environments increasingly shape people’s dietary choices. He said: “We cannot keep telling Nigerians to eat healthily while allowing unhealthy food and beverages to dominate our markets, schools, advertisements and public spaces. “Early action on diabetes must begin with enacting and implementing strong regulatory policies that make healthy choices possible, affordable and accessible, not simply with advising people to change their dietary behaviour.” The organisation cited its 2025 report, Junk On Our Plates, which documented aggressive marketing of ultra-processed foods and beverages high in sugar and sodium across seven Nigerian states. It said the report exposed the targeting of children, young people and low-income communities through advertising, celebrity endorsements, misleading nutrition labels and cultural imagery designed to promote unhealthy products. To reverse the trend, CAPPA outlined five major policy interventions, beginning with the conclusion and enforcement of the proposed Sugar-Sweetened Beverage (SSB) tax. It urged the House of Representatives and the Federal Executive to complete legislative action following the Senate’s passage of the tax review bill earlier this year. The organisation advocated an inflation-adjusted excise tax of at least 20 per cent

Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged politicians to keep politics away from places of worship, saying religious institutions should remain centres of spiritual growth and unity. Soludo made the call during a visit to the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention Deliverance Ministry Inc., Onitsha, to celebrate its 30th anniversary. The ministry was founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. He said: “Politicians, keep off places of worship! The governor described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that it marked maturity, preparation and a new phase in the ministry’s growth. He recalled that his first encounter with the ministry was during the demolition of part of its structure by the state government to facilitate the dredging of the Sakamori drainage channel. Soludo commended Odumeje for his contributions to charity and efforts towards societal development. He also acknowledged the cleric’s support for the state’s campaign against criminal idolatry and activities of illegal traditional spiritual practitioners. According to him, the advocacy, alongside the Anambra Homeland Security Law, has contributed to making the state safer. nigeria.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has assured residents of Abia State of improved security, pledging that the Nigeria Police Force would intensify efforts to protect lives and property across the state. Disu gave the assurance during a courtesy visit to Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia, where he commended the governor for his sustained support to the police. The IGP, who said he had received positive reports from the Commissioner of Police and the Assistant Inspector-General of Police on the state government’s assistance to the Force, promised that the police would reciprocate the gesture through improved service delivery. “I want to thank you for all you have been doing for my officers. The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, in honour of the personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident. He said the ceremony would also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the incident. On the recovery of the aircraft’s black box, Ejodame said the CVR, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site. He explained that data recovered from the voice recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to him, the investigation is progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA). The Air Force reiterated its commitment to ensuring that the investigation was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of professionalism, transparency, accountability and responsibility, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash. Ejodame further disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification process for the recovered remains was ongoing. He said the operation had been particularly challenging because of the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The NAF spokesman added that the Service was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. He said the Air Force recognised the grief of the bereaved families and remained committed to providing them with sustained support throughout the difficult period. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. sports.title: Cris Collinsworth says Bengals' fans are noticing Tee Higgins limping
sports.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins was injured during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. Higgins grabbed his leg after a catch, and went to the sideline. He limped noticeably after an incompletion shortly before halftime, but stayed in the game and had a 14-yard catch on the next play. "He has been limping a little bit, and I'm sure Bengals' fans are paying attention," NBC analyst Cris Collinsworth said during the broadcast. Higgins celebrated the 50th TD catch of his NFL career by handing the ball to an excited young fan during the team's NFL Week 9 win against Atlanta. Higgins helped teammate Ja'Marr Chase celebrate his touchdown with a nod to Spanish bullfighting . Higgins was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort in Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in NFL Week 8 against Tennessee. It was Higgins' first career AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 receiving yards against the Titans, and caught two of quarterback Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes . After being held without a catch during the first half, Higgins went off during the second half of a Week 7 rout in Baltimore, catching six Joe Burrow passes for 148 receiving yards with a touchdown. Earlier in the second half, Higgins' shoulder and arm were evaluated by medical personnel after he absorbed a big hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton after a catch. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. Against the Jaguars, Higgins got up slowly after a 19-yard catch near the sideline from Burrow . Higgins got up, but then took a knee. Higgins returned to the game later in the drive, and made a catch on his first play back in the game. He was not on the field for the Bengals' final drive of the game. Higgins had a game-high 10 catches for 140 receiving yards before the injury. He added a 17-yard catch, giving him a total of 157 receiving yards, second only to the 194-yard game he had against Baltimore in 2021. Higgins made a remarkable touchdown catch from quarterback Burrow late in the second quarter of the team's Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. It was among the most impressive NFL catches by Higgins . In March 2025, Higgins agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team. Higgins, Cincinnati's second-round pick in the 2020 NFL draft, is entering his seventh NFL season. sports.description: Louisville has a veteran-heavy team and when you have returning players it’s easy to compare them to seasons past. sports.description: NBC Sports analyst and former Cincinnati Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth blasted defensive back Jordan Battle for his unsportsmanlike conduct/ taunting penalty during the second quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' loss to Jacksonville because of a hamstring injury. Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. He played in all 51 of the Bengals' games over his first three seasons, recording six interceptions and making 30 starts. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of the Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss . Battle was injured during the fourth quarter of the Bengals' Week 13 loss to Pittsburgh last season. sports.title: St. Charles falls in OHSAA Division I boys soccer state final
sports.description: Another deep tournament run ended in unfortunately familiar fashion for the St. Charles soccer team. The Cardinals almost tripled Kettering Fairmont in shots and earned a handful of quality scoring chances in the Division I boys state final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, but the first-time state finalist Firebirds converted a higher percentage of opportunities and came away with a 3-1 win. Senior forward Sam Lofthouse scored St. Charles’ only goal, spinning and shooting from about 25 yards to the right of the goal with 25:35 to play and sneaking his shot into the upper right corner. That made it 2-1, but Fairmont (15-5-3) got the goal back less than four minutes later. Gavin Weaver’s corner kick got all the way through traffic, and Luke Davidson put it in from right in front. Azariyah Nsabimama and Aaron Black scored 12 minutes apart in the first half for Fairmont, and St. Charles lost for only the fourth time this season (18-4-1) and first since its regular-season finale Oct. 15 against Worthington Kilbourne. St. Charles, appearing in its 12th state tournament, fourth in a row and seeking its first title since 1985, outshot Fairmont 23-8. The Cardinals also were state runners-up in 2024, 2016, 1991, 1988 and 1981. St. Charles had outscored its first five tournament opponents 15-3, including a 1-0 win over defending state champion Dublin Jerome in a state semifinal in which Lofthouse had the only goal. Cardinals sophomore goalie Micah Neil made three saves. Fairmont’s Carson Dewald stopped six shots. This story will be updated. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. science.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972.
